input.question: Why is it such a "Taboo" to talk about how much you get paid at your job with co-workers?
input.ground_truth: Companies don't want you to know what everyone else makes. It's harder to value your own worth when you only know what you make. When people know what others make, they might be more likely to demand more. So, by making sure only you know how much you make (whether through contract language or through it being "frowned upon"), the company tends to get to pay people less

Question: Why is it such a "Taboo" to talk about how much you get paid at your job with co-workers?

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you and your friends at school all get some candies from your parents every week. Some kids might get more candies than others, and that’s okay! But if everyone started talking about exactly how many candies they got, some kids might feel sad if they got fewer, or maybe someone might get jealous or want to argue about it.

At work, people get paid money instead of candies. Sometimes, if everyone talks about how much money they get, it can make people feel uncomfortable or even cause arguments. That’s why grown-ups call it a “taboo”—it means it’s something we don’t usually talk about at work, so everyone can feel comfortable and get along better.

So, it’s like not talking about how many candies you have in front of your friends, to keep things happy and fair for everyone.
